title: Point-blowup factorization of a proper birational surface morphism
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be integral regular Noetherian schemes of dimension $2$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], with Noetherian meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and birational: there are dense open subschemes $V\subseteq X$ and $U\subseteq Y$ such that $f|_V$ factors through an isomorphism $V\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $f$ is a finite composition of blowups of reduced closed points [def-nagata-global-blowup]. A composition is understood up to isomorphism over $Y$; length zero is allowed, in which case $f$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-exceptional-curve-count] and put $r=|B(f)|$. Prove the assertion simultaneously for all proper birational morphisms of integral regular Noetherian surfaces by strong induction on $r$. The base $r=0$ says precisely that $f$ is an isomorphism, so the length-zero composition works. For the inductive step assume $r>0$ and the assertion for every such morphism with fewer contracted curves; choose $y\in Y\setminus U_f$. The same cited statement ensures that $y$ is closed and $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}=2$.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, first paragraph: induction on the number of curves in fibres, including the omitted finiteness and base-case details.

proof.text: Blow up the reduced point $y$, obtaining $b:Y'\to Y$. By [lem-sfb-regular-point-blowup-geometry], $Y'$ is integral regular Noetherian, $b$ is proper and is an isomorphism off $y$, and every closed point over $y$ has local dimension $2$. Thus $b$ is birational. It is surjective: its closed image contains the dense open $Y\setminus\{y\}$. Hence its fibre over $y$ is nonempty and has a closed point. Every closed point of $Y'$ has local dimension at most $2$, by the cited bound over $y$ and the isomorphism elsewhere; one over $y$ has local dimension $2$. The chain definition of dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] therefore gives $\dim Y'=2$. It remains to produce a lift $X\to Y'$.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, first paragraph and the point blowup used in the second paragraph.

proof.text: Set $U=X\setminus f^{-1}(y)$. This is dense because $f$ identifies dense opens and $y$ is a closed point of a surface. The inverse of $b$ away from $y$ defines a $Y$-morphism $U\to Y'$. Apply [lem-sfb-surface-rational-map-point-resolution] with base $Y$ and proper target $Y'\to Y$. Obtain a tower $X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=X$ and a $Y$-morphism $h:X_n\to Y'$. All its surfaces are integral regular Noetherian of dimension $2$; every centre lies over $y$. Choose a solution with $n$ minimal. Write $p_i:X_i\to X$ for the partial composites. Each point blowup is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], so all $p_i$ and $f p_i$ are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Each point blowup is an isomorphism over the complement of its centre by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], and every centre lies outside the inverse image of $U$; hence every $p_i$ is an isomorphism over the dense open $U$, and so is $f p_i$ over the dense open where $f$ is an isomorphism. They are therefore birational. In particular they are surjective, their images being closed and dense. Since $b$ is separated, [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] applied over $Y$ shows $h$ is proper; it is birational by the common dense open where both $b$ and $f p_n$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, second paragraph: resolve the rational lift by point blowups over the fibre.

proof.text: Suppose $n>0$, put $a:X_n\to X_{n-1}$, and denote its closed centre by $x$. Put $E=a^{-1}(x)$ and $F=b^{-1}(y)$. The morphism $a$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper] and an isomorphism over the dense open $X_{n-1}\setminus\{x\}$ by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], so its closed image is dense and $a$ is surjective; in particular $E$ is nonempty. As $x$ lies over $y$, the identity $b h=f p_n$ induces a morphism $v:E\to F$ of the scheme-theoretic fibres. If $v(E)$ contains more than one point, apply [lem-sfb-point-exceptional-isomorphism-neighbourhood] to the two point blowups $a,b$ and the proper birational map $h$. Its hypotheses hold even if $x$ has local dimension one: that lemma requires dimension two only at the target centre $y$. It gives $h^{-1}(|F|)=|E|$. Consequently the underlying fibre $(f p_n)^{-1}(y)$ is $|E|$. Surjectivity of $a$ then gives $(f p_{n-1})^{-1}(y)=\{x\}$, and surjectivity of $p_{n-1}$ gives $f^{-1}(y)=\{p_{n-1}(x)\}$.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, final three paragraphs: the nonconstant exceptional-image case forces a singleton original fibre.

proof.text: The singleton fibre in the preceding case contradicts the choice of $y$. Indeed $Y$ is normal by [rem-pc-regular-normal], and $X$ is reduced because it is integral. The dense-open isomorphism in the hypothesis identifies the unique generic points and their local fields, so it gives the birational hypothesis of [lem-sfb-normal-modification-codimension-one]. Clause (3) of that statement puts every point with a finite underlying fibre and normal target local ring into $U_f$. Thus $y\in U_f$, a contradiction. We conclude that the nonempty image $v(E)$ is a single point.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, final sentences: the finite-fibre clause of the normal modification criterion gives the contradiction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-point-blowdown-factorization] to $a:X_n\to X_{n-1}$ and $h:X_n\to Y'$. Since $h(E)$ is one point, obtain $h_{n-1}:X_{n-1}\to Y'$ with $h=h_{n-1}a$. This is a $Y$-morphism: the two maps $b h_{n-1}$ and $f p_{n-1}$ to $Y$ have the same composite with $a$, namely $f p_n$; uniqueness in the same blowdown-factorization statement identifies them. The tower of length $n-1$ with this map is therefore another solution, contradicting minimality. Hence $n=0$, and $h$ itself is the desired lift $g:X\to Y'$ with $f=b g$.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, second and third paragraphs: descend the final point blowup; minimality makes the induction on the source tower explicit.

proof.text: By [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target], the lift $g$ is proper, since $f$ is proper and $b$ is separated. It is birational on the dense open where $f$ and $b$ are isomorphisms. The schemes $X,Y'$ satisfy the surface hypotheses established above. By [lem-sfb-exceptional-curve-count], $B(g)\subsetneq B(f)$, so $|B(g)|<r$. The strong induction hypothesis gives a finite point-blowup factorization of $g$. Append the blowup $b$ at its target to obtain the required factorization of $f$. All compositions and the length-zero base case are understood up to isomorphism over the target, as in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0C5R, first paragraph: the strict decrease in contracted curves completes the outer induction.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0C5R (resolve-lemma-proper-birational-regular-surfaces), proof, with the omitted induction measure exposed as a separate node and source-tower induction made explicit by minimality.

lean.statement: theorem exists_point_blowup_factorization_of_proper_birational (X Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y] (hX : IsRegularScheme X) (hY : IsRegularScheme Y) (hdimX : topologicalKrullDim X = 2) (hdimY : topologicalKrullDim Y = 2) (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (hbirational : ∃ (V : X.Opens) (U : Y.Opens), Dense (V : Set X) ∧ Dense (U : Set Y) ∧ ∃ e : V.toScheme ≅ U.toScheme, V.ι ≫ f = e.hom ≫ U.ι) : ∃ (A : OrdinaryBlowupTower Y) (e : X ≅ A.level (Fin.last A.length)), e.hom ≫ A.toBase (Fin.last A.length) = f ∧ ∀ i : Fin A.length, ∃ (p : A.level i.castSucc) (hp : IsClosed ({p} : Set _)), A.center i = Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal ⟨{p}, hp⟩
